newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI cuts Bank Rate by one percentage point.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI cuts Bank Rate by one percentage point.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Wednesday it cut the Bank Rate to 10 percent per annum from 11 percent with effect from June 25.

"On a review of monetary and credit developments since the announcement of the monetary and credit policy in April 1997, the Reserve Bank of India has today decided to reduce the Bank Rate," the central bank said in a statement.
"With effect from the close of business today (June 25, 1997), the Bank Rate will be reduced by one percentage point, from 11 percent per annum to 10 percvent," it said.
The Bank Rate is the rate at which the central bank lends to commercial banks.
The RBI also announced a one percentage point cut to 8.0 percent per annum in interest rates on domestic term deposits with maturity from 30 days up to one year.
Rates on non-resident external rupee deposit accounts were also been reduced to 8.0 percent per annum, it said.
The central bank said it was also effecting a one percentage point cut in interest rates on post-shipment rupee export credit.

Interest rates on post-shipment export credit up to 90 days will now be "not exceeding 12 percent per annum" and that beyond 90 days and up to six months, 14 percent per annum, the RBI statement said.
All interest rates on advances from the RBI on export credit refinance and general refinance to banks which are specifically linked to the Bank Rate will also be revised downwards, it said.
